strings.name: Rose Marcario
strings.role: Former Patagonia president and CEO; Rivian Foundation trustees chair; REI director
strings.summary: Rose Marcario moved from finance and operations into outdoor apparel leadership, heading Patagonia and advancing environmental and civic participation initiatives. After leaving in 2020, she continued in corporate and nonprofit governance. In 2026 she left Rivian’s corporate board, remained chair of its foundation’s trustees and was elected to REI’s board.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Distinguishes Patagonia’s parent and apparel company, Rivian and its foundation, and announcement and effective dates; birth date remains unverified.
strings.influence.rationale: She led Patagonia and promoted environmental investment, responsible sourcing and corporate philanthropy.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: BSc in Business and Finance from SUNY Albany and MBA from California State University, Dominguez Hills; graduation years unverified.
strings.facts.f2.label: Earlier career
strings.facts.f2.value: Before joining Patagonia, she was CFO of General Magic and vice president of global finance and treasury at International Rectifier.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting business and environmental protection
strings.highlights.h1.text: At Patagonia she contributed to the food business, an internal investment fund and environmental initiatives, advancing corporate environmental responsibility.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Supporting civic participation
strings.highlights.h2.text: In 2018 she founded the Time to Vote business coalition, encouraging companies across party lines to promote voter participation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Recent conference retrospective published
strings.timeline.t1.text: Greater Purpose’s organizer recalled a conversation with her at its western conference; this is the article’s publication date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: REI announces board election results
strings.timeline.t2.text: Co-op members elected her to the board; the current roster also confirms her directorship.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Leaving Rivian’s corporate board
strings.timeline.t3.text: Her resignation submitted in December 2025 took effect, while she remained chair of the Rivian Foundation’s trustees.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joining Rivian’s board
strings.timeline.t4.text: She began serving as a director of the electric vehicle company, a role distinct from her foundation position.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Leaving Patagonia’s presidency and CEO role
strings.timeline.t5.text: Her departure was announced on June 10; operations chief Doug Freeman led the transition.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Founding Time to Vote
strings.timeline.t6.text: She encouraged companies to support employees’ participation in voting across party lines.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Additional Patagonia apparel CEO role announced
strings.timeline.t7.text: Already CEO of parent Patagonia Works, she was announced as also becoming president and CEO of Patagonia Inc.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joining Patagonia
strings.timeline.t8.text: She contributed to the company through finance and operations management before becoming CEO.
